recording.trigger: m (sustained motion, indoors, still on home Wi-Fi)
recording.note: raw file stays in the ignored data/raw tree; the site holds the same session

protocol: board carried by hand indoors: trigger walk, 2 min still, ~1.5 min normal walk, ~1 min fast walk, then still until the 5 min rule ended the session

thresholds.not_calibrated: run: nobody has run with the board; 600 mg is a guess above the ~610 mg transient seen when it was set down
thresholds.applies_to: this device and this mounting; a dog wearing it on a harness needs its own calibration

findings: rest and walk separate by a factor of about 25 (rest p90 4.2 mg, walk p10 102.9 mg), so the boundary is not sensitive: 149 of 149 labelled windows agreed

the dominant frequency is not a reliable cadence when the board is hand-carried: the normal-walk phase read 3.0-4.0 Hz (a harmonic) while the faster phase read 1.85 Hz, so classification uses amplitude only and the frequency is reported as a diagnostic
a single 610 mg window when the board was set down was classified as run; lone first/last windows now follow their neighbour
